questions.question_text: The water level in a canal lock reaches a maximum of $18.6$ m and a minimum of $5.4$ m. What are the amplitude and the mean position of a sinusoidal model of the level?

options.why: Used the full range $18.6-5.4$ as the amplitude instead of half of it.
Added the maximum and minimum for the mean position but forgot to divide by $2$.
Forgot to halve both the difference and the sum, so both values are doubled.

questions.solution_text:
$A=\dfrac{18.6-5.4}{2}$
$=\dfrac{13.2}{2}$
$=6.6$
$c=\dfrac{18.6+5.4}{2}$
$=\dfrac{24}{2}$
$=12$
The amplitude is $6.6$ m and the mean position is $12$ m.

questions.question_text:
Successive low tides at a beach are $14$ hours apart.
The depth is modelled by $y=k\cos(at)+c$, where $t$ is in hours.
What is the value of $a$?

options.why: Used $a=\dfrac{T}{2\pi}$ instead of $a=\dfrac{2\pi}{T}$.
Treated $14$ hours as half a period, so used $T=28$.
Both inverted the formula and treated $14$ hours as half a period.

questions.solution_text:
Successive low tides are one full period apart.
$T=14$
$a=\dfrac{2\pi}{T}$
$=\dfrac{2\pi}{14}$
$=\dfrac{\pi}{7}$

questions.question_text:
The height of a bicycle pedal above the ground is greatest at $32$ cm and least at $8$ cm, and the pedal completes one revolution every $2$ seconds.
The pedal is at its highest point when $t=0$ seconds.
Which model gives the height $h$ centimetres?

options.why: Chose the negative coefficient, which puts the minimum rather than the maximum at $t=0$.
Used the full range $32-8$ as the amplitude instead of half of it.
Used the full range as the amplitude and also chose the sign that puts the minimum at $t=0$.

questions.solution_text:
$A=\dfrac{32-8}{2}$
$=12$
$c=\dfrac{32+8}{2}$
$=20$
$a=\dfrac{2\pi}{2}$
$=\pi$
The pedal is at its maximum when $t=0$, so the coefficient of $\cos$ is positive.
$h=12\cos(\pi t)+20$

questions.question_text:
A carousel horse rises and falls between $0.8$ m and $1.6$ m above the platform, completing a cycle every $6$ seconds.
The horse is at its lowest point when $t=0$ seconds.
Which model gives the height $h$ metres?

options.why: Used a positive coefficient, which puts the maximum rather than the minimum at $t=0$.
Used the full range $1.6-0.8$ as the amplitude instead of half of it.
Used the full range as the amplitude and the sign that puts the maximum at $t=0$.

questions.solution_text:
$A=\dfrac{1.6-0.8}{2}$
$=0.4$
$c=\dfrac{1.6+0.8}{2}$
$=1.2$
$a=\dfrac{2\pi}{6}$
$=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$
The horse is at its minimum when $t=0$, so the coefficient of $\cos$ is negative.
$k=-0.4$
$h=-0.4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{3}\right)+1.2$

questions.question_text:
An alternating current swings between $-15$ A and $15$ A and completes $60$ cycles each second.
The current is $0$ and rising when $t=0$ seconds.
Which model gives the current $I$ amps?

options.why: Used the full range $15-(-15)$ as the amplitude instead of half of it.
Used the frequency $60$ as the period, giving $a=\dfrac{2\pi}{60}$.
Used the full range as the amplitude and the frequency as the period.

questions.solution_text:
$A=\dfrac{15-(-15)}{2}$
$=15$
$c=\dfrac{15+(-15)}{2}$
$=0$
$T=\dfrac{1}{60}$
$a=\dfrac{2\pi}{\frac{1}{60}}$
$=120\pi$
The current starts at the mean position and is rising, so use $\sin$ with a positive coefficient.
$I=15\sin(120\pi t)$

questions.question_text:
The possum population of a reserve varies between a high of $1750$ when monitoring begins and a low of $650$ eight months later. Successive highest populations are $16$ months apart.
Which model gives the population $P$ after $t$ months?

options.why: Used the full range $1750-650=1100$ as the amplitude instead of half of it.
Used the $8$ months from maximum to minimum as a full period instead of half a period.
Used the full range as the amplitude and the maximum-to-minimum interval as a full period.

questions.solution_text:
$A=\dfrac{1750-650}{2}$
$=550$
$c=\dfrac{1750+650}{2}$
$=1200$
The maximum-to-minimum interval is half a period, consistent with successive maxima being $16$ months apart.
$T=16$
$a=\dfrac{2\pi}{16}$
$=\dfrac{\pi}{8}$
The population starts at its maximum, so the coefficient of $\cos$ is positive.
$P=550\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{8}\right)+1200$

questions.question_text:
The depth of water at a beach ranges from $1.2$ m to $6.6$ m. The time from high tide to the very next low tide is $5$ hours.
The depth is greatest when $t=0$ hours.
Which model gives the depth $y$ metres?

options.why: Used the full range $6.6-1.2=5.4$ as the amplitude instead of half of it.
Used the $5$ hours from high tide to low tide as a full period instead of half a period.
Used a negative coefficient, which puts low tide rather than high tide at $t=0$.

questions.solution_text:
$A=\dfrac{6.6-1.2}{2}$
$=2.7$
$c=\dfrac{6.6+1.2}{2}$
$=3.9$
High tide to the next low tide is half a period.
$T=2\times5=10$
$a=\dfrac{2\pi}{10}$
$=\dfrac{\pi}{5}$
The depth starts at its maximum, so the coefficient of $\cos$ is positive.
$y=2.7\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{5}\right)+3.9$
